NJ-04.label: Absorption thin
NJ-04.text: With Arbor Terrace's 80 units counted, the project needs about 30% of unmet demand in a 7-mile market. Get a NIC MAP pull and a pre-leasing plan before LOI. Florham Park is the one Morris County pad to advance.

NJ-06.label: Hold: absorption
NJ-06.text: Arbor Terrace Florham Park (80 AL/MC, opening late 2027) uses up most of the unmet demand this pad needs. Hold behind Florham Park; do not pursue both.

NY-03.label: Partner role · needs PILOT
NY-03.text: VS Construction controls the site and Benchmark is the named operator (Planning Board, Feb 3 2026), so ATCO's role is capital or GC. Fully taxed YOC is 6.39% at norm lease-up; a PILOT lifts it to 7.28%.

NY-01.label: Pass as owner · fee development (pending Ben)
NY-01.text: At the slower lease-up, entrance-fee coverage falls to 70%, at the bottom of the screen, and a for-profit owner loses about $11.6M even with entrance fees. Owned by a nonprofit sponsor tax-exempt it makes about $21.4M, and ATCO earns about a $6.8M development fee plus the GC contract. Sunrise is the contract vendee.

NY-10.label: Needs PILOT
NY-10.text: At industry-norm lease-up (35 months), fully taxed YOC is 6.49%, a hair under the 6.5% floor. A Town of Poughkeepsie PILOT lifts it to 7.25%. Close only on a signed PILOT term sheet.

CT-02.label: Downside: fee development only
CT-02.text: Even with the PILOT and a GMP, the combined downside loses money for an owner. Only a nonprofit sponsor structure holds breakeven, with ATCO earning about a $4.8M development fee. Pursue it as fee development or as GC.

NJ-10.label: Downside needs a PILOT
NJ-10.text: Base case clears fully taxed, but the combined downside holds breakeven only with a GMP and a redevelopment-area PILOT, which the township has not designated. Ask about designation before LOI.
